about.title: Laguna Beach Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Laguna Beach's charm comes with tight, winding roads that see steady traffic year-round, and the most recent full-year data shows 155 injury collisions and 210 people hurt in and around town, with a concentration on Coast Highway, Laguna Canyon Road, and Route 133. Weekend afternoons, especially Saturdays between 2 and 4 p.m., tend to bring more reported crashes as beachgoers, commuters, and tourists share the same narrow corridors. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the choices you make in the first days matter: photographs of the scene, contact information for witnesses, and a written record of your symptoms can all support a claim later. Our team reviews what happened, explains your options under California law, and handles communication with insurers so you can focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Filing Clock Is Limited
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of a car accident to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — such as a city road authority — is involved. We can help identify which deadline applies to your situation early on.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash, though your share of fault may reduce the amount. Having someone evaluate the facts on your behalf can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often request a recorded statement soon after a crash, but anything you say can later be used to minimize your claim. Our team handles communication with the insurer for you so early statements don't undercut what you're owed, especially since California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering.

items.question: What should I do right after a crash on Coast Highway or Laguna Canyon Road?
items.answer: If you're able, document the scene with photos, get contact information from any witnesses, and seek medical attention even if injuries seem minor. Avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company until you've spoken with an attorney. Contact us, and our team can handle those conversations for you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Laguna Beach car accident?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That deadline can be much shorter, sometimes six months, if your claim involves a government entity, such as a city-maintained road. Because these timelines vary by circumstance, it's worth getting a case reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Will I still be able to recover damages if I was partly at fault?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California uses a pure comparative fault system, which allows injured people to recover a percentage of damages even if they share some responsibility for the accident. We can help present the facts in a way that fairly reflects what happened.

items.question: Does your firm charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No. Our initial case review is free, and we work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We'll evaluate your situation and explain your options under California law.
